problem_statement: The Interactive Points demo is a static Codrops experience (index.html + css/component.css + css/demo.css + js/main.js) that renders a London map with hover/click points, a sponsor block, a long-form content section and a related-demos section. A native POINT INDEX navigator (a normal-flow <nav class="pidx">) has been added above each of the two maps: it lists the six real map points (Rupert Street, Swiss Court, Bear Street, Leicester Square, Oxendon Street, Haymarket) as clickable cards, with a live readout that reads 'Awaiting selection - 6 points on the map' and, after a card is clicked, updates to 'Selecting: <name> - point N of 6'. Three regressions were introduced while wiring it up: (1) on a 390px mobile viewport the primary navigator's card row is a fixed-width no-wrap track that runs off the right edge and overflows the document horizontally; (2) the point cards collapse into an overlapping, illegible pile at desktop width because of negative margins and near-black-on-near-black text; and (3) after clicking a point card the readout no longer updates - it stays frozen on 'Awaiting selection'. The navigator above the SECOND map is also missing entirely. Repair css/pidx.css so the card row wraps and reads cleanly at every width, restore js/pidx.js so the readout reflects the clicked point live, and restore the POINT INDEX navigator above the second map so both maps carry it.
required_content: Fix css/pidx.css so the primary POINT INDEX card row does not cause horizontal overflow at 390px mobile width (documentElement / content right-edge stays within the viewport, tolerance 24px).
Fix css/pidx.css so the six point cards lay out cleanly side-by-side (or wrapped) at desktop width - no overlapping/shingled cards and no near-black-on-near-black illegible text.
Restore js/pidx.js so clicking a point card updates the readout live to 'Selecting: <name> - point N of 6' (e.g. clicking Bear Street shows 'Selecting: Bear Street - point 3 of 6').
Restore the POINT INDEX navigator above the SECOND map (#interactive-2) so both maps carry the navigator, matching the reference.
Keep all six point cards and their exact labels (Rupert Street, Swiss Court, Bear Street, Leicester Square, Oxendon Street, Haymarket) and the POINT INDEX heading rendered on every state.
Do not touch the interactive-points component, its hover/click point behaviour, js/main.js, or the static image assets.
design_constraints: The graded changes are limited to css/pidx.css (card row layout + card contrast) and js/pidx.js (readout wiring) plus the presence of the second-map navigator in index.html; the shared visual system in css/pidx.shared.css and all other files are unchanged.
Do not merely clip the overflow (overflow-x:hidden on a still-too-wide no-wrap row leaves the layout overflowing and the cards cut off); let the cards wrap or flex so the real content fits.

Preserve the navigator's visual look on desktop and tablet: the dark #28282f panel, the teal #60B8B9 uppercase POINT INDEX eyebrow, the rounded readout pill, the 1px bordered rounded cards, the two-line card layout (uppercase 'Point N' label above the point name), the card hover/active teal border highlight, and the consistent inter-card gap and padding.

The card row must lay the six cards out in a clean horizontal band (or wrap to multiple rows on narrow widths) with even spacing - no negative margins, no shingled/overlapping cards, no stacked z-index pile.
The readout must be recomputed from the clicked card on every click - do not snapshot the initial text and re-write that stale string.
The point cards must remain legible: the light card name text must contrast strongly against the dark card background (no near-black text on the near-black card).
state_constraints: desktop_initial loads the page at 1440px: the primary POINT INDEX navigator renders its six point cards in a clean readable row with no horizontal overflow.
mobile_initial checks the same page at 390px and MUST have no horizontal overflow (the repaired behaviour; the buggy baseline overflows here because of the fixed-width no-wrap card row).
tablet_initial checks the same page at 834px and preserves the original tablet layout.
desktop_point_pick clicks the Bear Street point card in the primary navigator; the readout updates to 'Selecting: Bear Street - point 3 of 6' (frozen on the buggy wiring).
desktop_second_map scrolls to the second map (#interactive-2); the POINT INDEX navigator is present above it in the reference (absent in the buggy baseline).
mobile_point_index checks the primary navigator at 390px with no horizontal overflow.

change_completion: The primary POINT INDEX card row no longer causes horizontal overflow at 390px mobile.
Clicking a point card updates the readout live to 'Selecting: <name> - point N of 6', and the navigator is restored above the second map.
design_consistency: The navigator keeps its dark-panel, teal-eyebrow, bordered-card visual system on desktop and tablet.
The point cards lay out cleanly (no overlap/shingling) with legible card text.
responsive: The card row wraps or flexes so mobile (390px) shows no horizontal overflow.
The tablet (834px) layout is preserved with no overflow.
regression: No regression: the page MUST preserve its Codrops header, BOTH interactive-points map components (#interactive-1 and #interactive-2), the sponsor block, the long-form content section, and the related-demos section, all rendered exactly as before the change.

No regression in behaviour or assets: js/main.js, the interactive-points hover/click point behaviour, the six background images and img/map.png are unchanged and still function; the repair must not remove, hide, shorten, or restyle any pre-existing page content.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: codrops/InteractivePoints is a runnable static HTML/CSS/JS Codrops demo (a London interactive-points map) served directly with a static file server. Its genre-native interactive control is a POINT INDEX navigator over the six map points - a wayfinding rail with clickable point cards and a live selection readout. That makes it an ideal L4 target: the reference wraps the card row (0 mobile overflow), lays the cards out legibly, wires the readout live and renders the navigator over both maps; the buggy baseline keeps the fixed-width no-wrap row (mobile overflow) and drops the second-map navigator; the negative-control 'bad' additionally shingles the cards into an illegible overlap and freezes the readout.

author_notes: Rebuilt to product-grade L4 with a native POINT INDEX navigator (the demo's own map point-navigation control), replacing the earlier passive itinerary strip. Four orthogonal gates: D6 no_horizontal_overflow (mobile_initial, tol 24) on the primary navigator card row; D3 visual_regression (desktop_initial + mobile_initial) catching the collapsed/illegible broken card layout on bad via pixelmatch + ssim + block_fidelity over the navigator crop; D2 dom_assertions (desktop_second_map) on the pidx--secondary navigator presence; D4 interaction_assertions (desktop_point_pick) on the live 'Selecting: Bear Street - point 3 of 6' readout. Graded files: css/pidx.css, js/pidx.js, index.html (second-map navigator). Shared css/pidx.shared.css and the map image assets (img/map.png, img/1.jpg) are INFRA. Runtime clean (0 console / 0 network) on every state and leg. Distinct strip from same-repo slot_246 (a POINT ASSET LEDGER); slot_246 has since moved to a different repo.
